short: A series of dynastic civil wars for the throne of England fought between the rival houses of Lancaster and York.
full:
Fought intermittently between 1455 and 1487, the Wars of the Roses pitted supporters of two rival cadet branches of the royal House of Plantagenet against one another. The conflict was rooted in the weak rule of Henry VI, economic troubles, and the dynastic claims of Richard, Duke of York.

The wars saw sudden reversals of fortune, multiple usurpations, and severe attrition among the English aristocracy. They effectively concluded with the victory of Henry Tudor over Richard III at Bosworth Field in 1485, followed by the suppression of the final Yorkist rebellion at Stoke Field in 1487. Henry VII's marriage to Elizabeth of York united the two houses and established the Tudor dynasty, ending the medieval period in England.
